docs.title: Welcome
docs.text:
EGR 304 (Michael Kim) Datasheet as part of Automated Plant Irrigation System for Team 211

Submission: December 08, 2025

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: This website holds all the data and processes from my individual part of the EGR 304 M/W 1:30 pm section of Team 211. The main team project aims to assist homeowners with plant care, so my system is designed to complement the motor and speakers used in the team project.

docs.title: Project Summary
docs.text: For the project, my board includes a Solenoid valve and a Speaker system, so I am supposed to receive two signals (one power and one analog) from the main board. The analog signal goes to the speaker to allow for more diverse sounds and alarms, while the power opens the solenoid. You can read more from the team report.

docs.title: My Contribution
docs.text:
For the team component, I was one of the subsystems of the main board. I was responsible for the design and creation of the solenoid and speaker system.

To review the details of the data sheet, hyperlinks are provided below: 1. Block Diagram 2. Component Selection 3. BOM 4. Schematic 5. Power Budget 6. PCB Design 7. Microcontroller Code

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The purpose of a block diagram is to help with the connections of the system. In a block diagram, one can give a person a reasonable outline about why a part was chosen based on power levels, whether it was a sensor or an actuator. A block diagram also helps with our team project, which shows you where each board will be connected with the other team members.

docs.title: Solenoid Motor
docs.text:
Solution Pros Cons Option 1. Plastic Water Solenoid Valve - 12V - 1/2" Nominal $6.95/eachlink to product * Inexpensive * Compatible with PSoC * Requires external components and support circuitry for interface* Needs special PCB layout. * Option 2. * 12V Solenoid Valve - 3/4" - 1046 * $9.62/each * Link to product * Smaller * Operates at 0.2~8 bar * 0°C ~ 75°C *Tariff May Apply * Option 3. * DFRobot FIT0617 Solenoid Valve * $25/each * Link to product * Direct connection to Microcontroller * Valve and DC Motor integrated * Larger Size *Estimated 44% Tariff

Rationale: Because we didn't use most of the budget on the Speaker, I think we can spend some here to get a really plug-and-play solenoid motor that fits directly with the PIC Nano.

All in all, Option 1 is the easiest because I already have it on hand. However, option 1 is not available right now, so option 3 is better.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The zip file showing you my code for the microcontroller is here.

The code is set to toggle an LED back and forth on pin RF3 and use a speaker when receiving an input. How this is done is this board recieves a digital input from the main board and receives in pin RD6, then I run a DAC (Digital to Analog Conversion) and output an analog signal to pin RA2. I then have a square wave that plays a sound.
